newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah regains ground, but still soft.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah regains ground, but still soft.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah regained some ground against the dollar in late afternoon trading on Wednesday, but overall tone on the rupiah remained soft, dealers said.
They said trading was a bit slow, with Singapore players seen driving the dollar up in the morning on short-covering due to a public holiday over there, aided by ample money supply.
But late profit-taking helped the rupiah recover slightly.
Spot rupiah was at 2,431.5/32.5 at 0910 GMT after falling to a low of 2,434 from an opening of 2,426.5/27.5.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,431.0/32.0 and 2,430.5/31.5, respectively.
"It's a bit of a directionless market. We just go with the market," one Japanese bank dealer said.
Another dealer said the ample rupiah market, with overnight money falling to seven percent, was supporting the dollar's upturn.
One dealer said earlier the market was liquidity-driven, reflected by relatively steady longer-term swap rates as operators maintained short dollar outright positions.
He said dollar's rise triggered stop-loss buying but this met strong dollar resistance at the 2,434.0 level.
Dealers said the underlying tone remained biddish for the dollar in the short-term as election campaign proceeds.
Indonesia's election campaign, which will last until May 23 ahead of the May 29 poll, started smoothly on Sunday helping to calm the market.
However, dealers said the market would remain cautious for the next two weeks.
Overnight swap was at 0.35/0.42 and tom/next at 0.37/0.45.
One-month swaps were at 12.5/13.0, two at 24.5/25.5, three at 37.75/38.75 and six at 75.00/75.75 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,407/2,599 and the conversion band to 2,409/2,457 on Wednesday.
